decisions.decision: Use a committed file for observations instead of generating it in tests.
decisions.rationale: Two test binaries were writing to the same temporary file concurrently, causing a race condition where one truncated the file while the other read it. A committed file cannot race.
decisions.quote: The repair is that the observations are a committed file

decisions.decision: Add the new observations fixture to the examples.
decisions.rationale: The fixture is a demonstrable example and can be generated into the manual alongside the rest.
decisions.quote: 37 worked examples now, because the fixture is a demonstrable example

decisions.decision: Do not fit the residuals in the example.
decisions.rationale: Extracting a quadratic trend is least squares, and a reader needs to know which code produced the number, so it is not produced here.
decisions.quote: which code produced the number, so it is not produced here.

decisions.decision: Use synthetic observations moved by known amounts.
decisions.rationale: The residuals are known in advance and the arithmetic can be checked by eye.
decisions.quote: so the residuals are known in advance and the arithmetic can be checked by eye.

decisions.decision: Include an observation outside its window.
decisions.rationale: This demonstrates the property that the width exists to carry, which grows with the cycle.
decisions.quote: which is the point of carrying a width that grows with the cycle.

prerequisites.text: Reading no observations is an error, not a report of agreement.

alternatives.alternative: Writing the fixture into `std::env::temp_dir()` under a fixed name.
alternatives.reason: Two test binaries ran concurrently, causing one to truncate the file while the other read it.
alternatives.quote: The first version wrote one into `std::env::temp_dir()` under a fixed name, and this file and `manual_fields.rs` both did it — two test binaries, one path, run concurrently. One truncated the file while the other read it

alternatives.alternative: Extracting a quadratic trend using least squares.
alternatives.reason: A reader most needs to know which code produced the number.
alternatives.quote: **This reports and does not fit.** A quadratic trend in these residuals is `Ṗ`, and extracting it is least squares — which is where a reader most needs to know which code produced the number, so it is not produced here.

consequences.text: Fixes a race condition where concurrent tests truncated and read the same temporary file.
consequences.quote: One truncated the file while the other read it, so the read saw nothing

consequences.text: The fixture becomes a demonstrable example generated into the manual alongside the rest.
consequences.quote: the fixture is a demonstrable example and is generated into the manual alongside the rest.

consequences.text: Avoids producing a least squares fit where the reader wouldn't know which code produced it.
